newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares steam ahead, target life high.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares steam ahead, target life high.

text.p: Austria's ATX index powered higher on Friday, breaching resistance at 1,227 and set its sights on the life high of 1,261.16.
The blue chip ATX index rose 13.83 points or 1.13 percent to 1,241.04. Among its constituents 14 shares rose, six fell and one was unchanged.
Traders said fresh demand for market heavyweight OMV, which closed at a new year high, was behind the rise. Prices were further underpinned by the firm overnight close on Wall Street, they added.
"The climb was driven by a few individual titles, above all OMV," said one trader.
In spite of going ex-dividend, energy and chemicals group OMV, shot to a new high of 1,500 schillings before ending slightly lower at 1,495 schillings, up 3.25 percent.

"The interest rate situation is fine and the mood in the economy is positive," said another trader, who thought another stab at the historic high of 1,261.06 points on March 11 this year was not impossible in the near future.
Demand was particularly strong in cyclical stocks, but the market still lacked broad interest, he noted.
The top gainer was steel firm VA Stahl jumping 3.41 percent to 515 schillings.
Insurer EA-Generali was the biggest decliner, dropping 1.28 percent to 3,080 schillings.
The May ATX futures contract gained 19.3 points to end at 1,239.9. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 257
